summary: The two disciples hurry back from Emmaus to Jerusalem and find the eleven already saying that the Lord is risen and has appeared to Simon.
key_insight: The two ran back with news, and news was waiting for them. Before they told their story, they heard that Jesus had appeared to Simon. Two separate testimonies, from two different places, met in one room and confirmed each other.
story: The two disciples rose up that very hour and set out for Jerusalem, back along the same seven miles, though the day was already far spent.
In the city they found the eleven and those who were with them gathered together, saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”
Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how He was known to them in the breaking of bread.

scene.label: A night journey
scene.text: The two had urged their guest to stay because evening was coming. Now they made the return trip in the dark. Travel at night was slow and less safe, but the news would not wait until morning.

scene.label: Those who were with them
scene.text: Luke says the eleven were not alone. Other followers were gathered with them, probably including the women who had gone to the tomb. A few weeks later Luke counts about a hundred and twenty believers in Jerusalem (Acts 1:15).

scene.label: The breaking of bread
scene.text: A Jewish meal began when the host gave thanks, broke the bread and handed it around. Luke uses the same phrase for the gatherings of the early church (Acts 2:42; 20:7).

scene.label: Two witnesses
scene.text: The law said that a matter was established “by the mouth of two or three witnesses” (Deuteronomy 19:15). That evening, testimony came from two directions at once: from Simon Peter, and from the two who had walked to Emmaus.

witnesses.luke: Luke alone records this meeting, and he uses it to join two lines of testimony: the eleven already had Peter’s word, and the two brought theirs. Luke wrote so that Theophilus might “know the certainty” of what he had been taught (1:4), and here he shows witnesses confirming one another.

seeing.reveals: Jesus made Himself known to more than one person, in more than one place, on the same day. His resurrection rests on witnesses who confirmed each other, not on one person’s private experience.
seeing.living: The two could have stayed in Emmaus for the night and kept their joy to themselves. They went straight back to the company of disciples, told what Jesus had done, and heard what He had done for Peter. Bring what Jesus has shown you to His people, and listen to what He has shown them.
seeing.ponder: Who needs to hear how Jesus has made Himself known to you, and whose story of His faithfulness might strengthen your own faith?

preaching.big_idea: When Jesus meets us, we run to His people and find He has met them too.
outline: Hearing that the Lord is risen (34)
preaching.watch_for: On the road, the two called Jesus “a Prophet mighty in deed and word” (24:19). Now the gathered disciples call Him “the Lord.” The day has moved them from a prophet who died to the Lord who is risen.

title: The Emmaus Disciples Return
